an3.27:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an3.27:1.3: (1) There is a person who is to be looked upon with disgust, not to be associated with, followed, and served;
an3.27:1.4: (2) a person who is to be looked upon with equanimity, not to be associated with, followed, and served;
an3.27:1.5: and (3) a person who is to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:1.6: (1) “And what kind of person, bhikkhus, is to be looked upon with disgust, not to be associated with, followed, and served?
an3.27:1.7: Here, some person is immoral, of bad character, impure, of suspect behavior, secretive in his actions, not an ascetic though claiming to be one, not a celibate though claiming to be one, inwardly rotten, corrupt, depraved.
an3.27:1.8: Such a person is to be looked upon with disgust, not to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:1.10: Even though one does not follow the example of such a person, a bad report still circulates about oneself:
an3.27:1.11: ‘He has bad friends, bad companions, bad comrades.’
an3.27:1.12: Just as a snake that has passed through feces, though it does not bite one, would smear one,
an3.27:1.13: so too, though one does not follow the example of such a person, a bad report still circulates about oneself:
an3.27:1.14: ‘He has bad friends, bad companions, bad comrades.’
an3.27:1.15: Therefore such a person is to be looked upon with disgust, not to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:2.1: (2) “And what kind of person is to be looked upon with equanimity, not to be associated with, followed, and served?
an3.27:2.3: Here, some person is prone to anger and easily exasperated. Even if he is criticized slightly he loses his temper and becomes irritated, hostile, and stubborn; he displays irritation, hatred, and bitterness.
an3.27:2.4: Just as a festering sore, if struck by a stick or a shard, will discharge even more matter, so too …
an3.27:2.6: Just as a firebrand of the tinduka tree, if struck by a stick or shard, will sizzle and crackle even more, so too …
an3.27:2.8: Just as a pit of feces, if struck by a stick or a shard, becomes even more foul-smelling,
an3.27:2.10: so too some person here is prone to anger and … displays irritation, hatred, and bitterness.
an3.27:2.11: Such a person is to be looked upon with equanimity, not to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:2.13: With the thought: ‘He might insult me, revile me, and do me harm.’
an3.27:2.14: Therefore such a person is to be looked upon with equanimity, not to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:3.1: (3) “And what kind of person is to be associated with, followed, and served?
an3.27:3.2: Here, some person is virtuous and of good character.
an3.27:3.3: Such a person is to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:3.5: Even though one does not follow the example of such a person, a good report still circulates about oneself:
an3.27:3.6: ‘He has good friends, good companions, good comrades.’
an3.27:3.7: Therefore such a person is to be associated with, followed, and served.
an3.27:3.8: “These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
an3.27:4.2: A verse is attached identical with that in 3:26.
